lead.headline: Russian missiles and drones kill at least 11 across Ukraine overnight
lead.dek: A five-story apartment block in Pryluky was destroyed; Zelensky calls the strike a birthday 'gift' to Putin
body: Russia fired dozens of missiles and 130 drones at Ukrainian cities overnight into Wednesday, killing at least 11 people and destroying a five-story apartment building in Pryluky, in the northern Chernihiv region, Ukrainian officials said, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky called one of the biggest attacks since the full-scale invasion began in 2022.

Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 48 cruise missiles, an unspecified number of ballistic missiles and 130 drones, and that air defenses downed 161 of them. Interior Minister Ihor Vyhivskyi said nine people, including three children, were killed in Pryluky; Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said two died in a fire in the city's Darnytskyi district.

Russia's Defense Ministry said it carried out a "massive strike" on military-industrial sites in Kyiv and other regions, including plants making Flamingo cruise missiles, and on Odesa port facilities; it did not mention civilian casualties. The attack fell on Putin's 74th birthday and followed drone strikes Tuesday on two cargo ships off Bulgaria, one of which sank.

briefs.headline: Paramount closes $110B Warner Bros. deal; shares trade as SKYD
briefs.summary: The merger, completed Tuesday, unites CBS News and CNN, Paramount+ and HBO Max; co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz target $6 billion in savings.

briefs.headline: Christa Pike conscious, speaking after failed execution
briefs.summary: Attorneys said the Tennessee inmate, 50, who survived two doses of pentobarbital Sept. 30, remains shackled to a hospital bed; her prognosis is unclear.

briefs.headline: Collins, Jackson clash over Trump in first Maine debate
briefs.summary: Jackson named Trump at least 20 times in the hour-long WGME debate Tuesday; Collins, seeking a sixth term, said she is "not exactly his favorite senator."

briefs.headline: Ex-CIA officer found with $40M in gold pleads guilty
briefs.summary: David Rush, 49, admitted wire fraud in Alexandria, Va., Tuesday and agreed to forfeit at least $194 million, including gold bars and four Florida homes; sentencing is Jan. 28.

briefs.headline: Ex-BND chief Hanning arrested on espionage suspicion
briefs.summary: Federal prosecutors said the 80-year-old, who led the BND from 1998 to 2005, is suspected of obtaining state secrets via his former chief of staff.

briefs.headline: Houthis hit Aden airport; Saudis down missile near Riyadh
briefs.summary: Yemen's transport ministry said missiles and drones targeted Aden's runway and terminal early Wednesday; Saudi Arabia said it intercepted a missile north of Riyadh.

briefs.headline: Takaichi meets Okinawa governor as U.S. military pauses
briefs.summary: U.S. forces on Okinawa paused operations for two days, with a 30-day curfew to follow, after the Marine's murder arrest; Gov. Genta Koja cited "great shock and anxiety."

briefs.headline: Kenya confirms first Ebola case and death
briefs.summary: Health Minister Aden Duale said a Kenyan who had been living in Congo flew in from Kampala Saturday, tested positive and died late Monday at Nairobi Hospital.

briefs.headline: Officials urge nuclear pursuit after state exits hub program
briefs.summary: The state was one of six finalists for the federal Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses program before the Morrisey administration opted out by letter last week, MetroNews reported; Treasurer Larry Pack called it a setback.

briefs.headline: WVU issues campus warning after fraternity hazing reports
briefs.summary: University police issued the Clery Act warning Tuesday after anonymous reports of alleged hazing at at least two on-campus fraternity sites; WVU said criminal investigations are active.

briefs.headline: Three Wyoming County schools stay closed through Friday
briefs.summary: Wyoming East, Westside and Mullens Elementary-Middle remain closed for professional cleaning after students developed a skin rash Monday; the county's other schools reopen Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Woody Williams statue commission holds first meeting
briefs.summary: The commission met Tuesday at the Capitol; the statue would replace John Kenna's in the U.S. Capitol's National Statuary Hall, with Kenna's moved to the Culture Center in Charleston.

regional.item: Milton council passed first reading Tuesday of rules requiring approval and public input before buying Flock-style surveillance tech.
Charleston council Monday approved transferring the former West Side Save-A-Lot to Mountaineer Food Bank for a volunteer hub.
Samantha Deem, charged with murder in Monday's 7th Street shooting, is set for arraignment Oct. 14, the News and Sentinel reported.
A second air test at Webster County High found no mold, Superintendent Joseph Arbogast told the board Sept. 28, the Echo reported Tuesday.

away.item: Bennington's Select Board voted 5-1 Monday to put $1.25 million of an estimated $1.8 million in first-year option-tax revenue toward the general fund if voters approve the 1% tax Nov. 3.

hotspots.item: A $500 mini grant will keep two Main Street streetlights and a park floodlight on in Camden-on-Gauley for about seven months, the Echo reported Tuesday.
North Topsail Beach aldermen meet at 11 a.m. today on a $200,000 Town Hall decking rehab, a $65,000 Beach Access 18 replacement and a $50,000 NCDOT crosswalk contract.

briefs.headline: Eight PG mayoral hopefuls face 'job interview' forum at UNBC
briefs.summary: Eight Prince George mayoral candidates took 10-minute turns on public safety, infrastructure and reconciliation at the UNBC-Chamber forum Tuesday night; Keenan Murphy did not attend.

briefs.headline: Prince George council orders review of cremation capacity
briefs.summary: Council voted Monday to have staff assess the city's cremation capacity and consult faith groups and funeral homes, reporting to the council elected Oct. 17.

briefs.headline: B.C. Conservatives would restore right to sue after crashes
briefs.summary: A Sept. 29 letter from Lorne Doerkson, leaked by the ICBC workers' union, pledges a hybrid system letting seriously injured victims sue; David Eby called it a "secret deal" with trial lawyers.

briefs.headline: FBI complaint details Tumbler Ridge shooter's guns
briefs.summary: The complaint against James Bryant, 30, of Bellingham, charged Tuesday with conspiracy to murder, says Jesse Van Rootselaar took guns from her family's safe, one once seized by RCMP.

briefs.headline: Plamondon says referendum is not an immediate priority
briefs.summary: The Quebec premier-designate said Tuesday his 59-seat PQ minority will start with a homelessness summit and a spending review, and that a sovereignty vote will not come while Trump is in office.

briefs.headline: Ottawa gives Stelco's U.S. owner five days to save jobs
briefs.summary: Industry Minister Melanie Joly's Monday letter warns Cleveland-Cliffs it could face court action under the Investment Canada Act over up to 500 layoffs at the Hamilton steelmaker.

briefs.headline: Kagan and Soai win chemistry Nobel for chirality work
briefs.summary: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won for discovering non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis, the academy said Wednesday; they share 12 million kronor.

briefs.headline: Stanford team regrows knee cartilage in old mice
briefs.summary: Blocking the enzyme 15-PGDH restored lost cartilage in aged mice and prevented arthritis after an ACL-like injury, Stanford Medicine reported in Science.

briefs.headline: Pennsylvania measles cases pass 1,000 for the year
briefs.summary: The state health department confirmed 1,004 cases Monday, up 106 in a week, with 198 hospitalizations; more than 99% of patients were unvaccinated.

briefs.headline: MIT physicists see quarks make wakes in plasma
briefs.summary: CMS data from CERN's Large Hadron Collider gave the first direct evidence that quark-gluon plasma responds to fast quarks, a team led by MIT reported in Physics Letters B.

briefs.headline: Mistral's trillion-parameter model trails U.S. leaders
briefs.summary: Mistral Large 4 scored 38 on Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index, up from 9 for Large 3, against 58 for the leading Claude Opus 5.5 configuration, The Decoder reported.

briefs.headline: Sony seeks takedown of 260,000 AI deepfake songs
briefs.summary: The label's request is nearly double the 135,000 takedowns it had previously sought for tracks imitating its artists, The Verge reported, citing the Financial Times.

briefs.headline: Researchers track a Chinese AI agent fleet online
briefs.summary: Independent researchers reported Sunday that agents appearing to run on Tencent infrastructure queried Alibaba's Amap service, sidestepping its API rules, TechCrunch said.

weather_ear: Wednesday's forecast follows at 7:15, from the weather desk.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster carries a regional line for the first time in six mornings; Crew-12 is due to undock at 8:05 a.m. and splash down Thursday.
